name: Solberg-Maru Thermal Work Layer
description:
Solberg-Maru makes workwear for people who spend time in cold industrial environments — the kind of cold that comes from unheated warehouses, exposed infrastructure catwalks, or the Lake Erie waterfront from November through April. Their thermal work layer is a fitted crew-neck shirt in brushed synthetic fleece-back jersey, designed to be worn under a jacket or hi-vis vest without bunching. The exterior is smooth enough to slide under outerwear; the interior is deeply brushed and traps heat efficiently. Reinforced panels run along the forearms and across the upper back — these areas get the most friction from tools, harnesses, and machinery.

Available in safety orange, slate, and a dark olive. No branding on the front — just a small woven label at the inside collar. The stitching at the cuffs is doubled and uses a stretch-resistant thread that doesn't fail when you're gripping something cold. This is a shirt that has never once been worn to a party and doesn't need to be.
what_it_says: You work outside or in unheated industrial spaces and you've learned to dress for it. Practical without being showy. The kind of competence that doesn't announce itself.
story_hooks: A Solberg-Maru thermal was found at the bottom of a Lake Erie maintenance shaft — still on a body that officially drowned in a district three kilometers away.
The dark olive colorway was discontinued after a specific incident involving a work crew that hasn't been publicly explained; the remaining stock commands a strange premium among people who know.
A Tier 3 organizer uses the Solberg-Maru as a way to move through Tier 2 industrial zones without drawing attention — but someone has started noticing the pattern.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian fitted crew-neck thermal shirt with a distinctly industrial aesthetic. Sits close to the torso without compression, allowing freedom of movement under outer layers. The brushed interior creates subtle texture depth visible at neckline and cuffs. Reads as pure function—no style flourishes, no attitude.
physical_description.fit: Fitted but not tight; cut to accommodate a standard working frame with room for arm movement. Tapers slightly at the waist. Sleeves are precisely proportioned to end at the wrist without excess fabric. Designed to layer invisibly under jackets and hi-vis vests.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed synthetic fleece-back jersey. Exterior: smooth, dense knit for glide under outerwear. Interior: deep pile brushed fleece for thermal retention and moisture wicking.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost slick exterior with faint knit grid pattern. Interior features pronounced brushed pile that catches light softly. Cuff seams are visibly reinforced with crisp, flat-locked stitching.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in safety orange (high-visibility standard), slate gray (neutral industrial), and dark olive (low-profile variant). No patterns or graphics; solid colorways only.
physical_description.closures: None—pull-over crew-neck construction. No fasteners or zippers.
distinctive_features: Reinforced forearm panels in double-layer construction
Upper back reinforcement panel for harness and load contact zones
Doubled, stretch-resistant stitching at cuffs—engineered for repeated gripping of cold objects
Small woven manufacturer label at inside collar only—no exterior branding
Flat-lock seams to prevent snag points on machinery or tools
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional workwear. Solberg-Maru positions at accessible working-class price point with industrial-grade durability. Not luxury, not salvage—reliable infrastructure.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by warehouse workers, dock handlers, infrastructure maintenance crews, GLMZ waterfront laborers, and Iowan Behemoth supervisors who work in unheated zones. Signals competence, exposure to genuine weather, physical labor. Worn by people who cannot afford to be cold and have no sympathy for aesthetics.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but not destroyed. Minor pilling from repeated friction, possible faint stains from machine oil or rust water. Cuffs show wear from constant contact with tools and metal surfaces. Interior brushing remains fully functional even after 200+ wash cycles. Never pristine; always worked.

image_prompt: A Tier 3 industrial worker wearing a fitted safety orange Solberg-Maru thermal layer, photographed against a backdrop of corroded metal warehouse scaffolding. Moody sodium-vapor warehouse lighting casts sickly gold shadows across the fabric. The model's forearm reinforcement panels are subtly visible, catching light to show the double-layer construction. Close detail shot of the cuff stitching and brushed interior texture near the neckline. Dark, utilitarian, no lifestyle styling—this is equipment, not fashion. Shot from front and side angles showing the fitted silhouette under a semi-transparent hi-vis vest. Desaturated color palette with accent on the orange. Cyberpunk industrial aesthetic, Lake Erie waterfront morning atmosphere. --ar 2:3 --v 6
